entries.title: Arrival
entries.text: I came through the gate my grandmother built. Most of it was lying in the grass.

entries.title: Tendai
entries.text: Tendai has kept this place for thirty-one years, the last eight alone. He talks like the land owes him nothing and he owes it everything.

entries.title: The gate shuts
entries.text: Mended the main gate today. Tendai swung it open and shut three times, just to hear it.

entries.title: They came back
entries.text: Impala at Waterhole A this morning. A few dozen, nervous, but there.

entries.title: Around the fire
entries.text: The pump died, then the drought, then the wages, then the rangers. Then the snares. Gran never sold.

entries.title: Ruin, survived
entries.text: Water in the ground, a gate that shuts. Tendai thinks the old pump didn't die on its own.

entries.title: Foundations
entries.text: Today we start building something that lasts.

entries.title: The list
entries.text: Find out what killed the pump. Build a new one. Hire a ranger. Stop losing money. Mend the west fence for the river.

entries.title: Cut, not broken
entries.text: The pump's main pipe was sawn through. Someone wanted it to look like it failed.

entries.title: Tracks in the clay
entries.text: A heavy vehicle came in from the east road, to the pump and back, never through the gate. Expensive city cigarettes.

entries.title: Gran's logbook
entries.text: “Mr H. visited again. Third offer. Told him no.” Two days later the pump was dead.

entries.title: Not bad luck
entries.text: The pump was sabotaged two days after Gran refused Mr H. a third time. We can't prove it. Yet.

entries.title: The pump sings
entries.text: New borehole pump running. Tendai stood next to it for an hour, just listening.

entries.title: Help arrives
entries.text: Hired our first ranger. Tendai pretended not to be pleased.

entries.title: The river
entries.text: Mended the west fence. The River & Wetland is part of the reserve again. Gran called it the reserve's memory.

entries.title: Two letters
entries.text: An ecologist wants to count our impala. And someone called V. Hale wants to be our partner.

entries.title: Too many mouths
entries.text: Water brought the herds back. Now there are more impala than the plains can feed.

entries.title: Dr. Okafor
entries.text: Amara arrived with a clipboard and two tally counters. She counts everything, including my mistakes.

entries.title: Wanjiru
entries.text: Our elephants ate three families' maize. Wanjiru came to the gate and told me exactly what she thought of that.

entries.title: The plan
entries.text: We argued until midnight about the impala. I made the call. Now I have to live with it.

entries.title: The village
entries.text: I walked to the village and gave Wanjiru my answer. She said her people watch what we do, not what we say.

entries.title: Down to size
entries.text: The impala are down to what the land can carry. The grass has a chance now.

entries.title: New wire
entries.text: Tendai found a line of snares in the woodland. New wire. Somebody is organised, and somebody is paying.

entries.title: A season's work
entries.text: Green at the edges again. Amara is staying. Tendai says it's time for visitors.

entries.title: The woodland
entries.text: The woodland fence is mended. Shade, birdsong, and a lot of places to hide.

entries.title: The eastern border
entries.text: The east side of the reserve is open again, right up to the village fields.

entries.title: Growth
entries.text: The reserve is alive again. Now it has to pay its way.

entries.title: Cars at the gate
entries.text: Three cars came today, just to look. Tendai counted them twice.

entries.title: First visitors
entries.text: A little girl saw her first lion from our tower. She asked if she could come back tomorrow.

entries.title: Coming home
entries.text: A reserve up north can spare giraffe and wildebeest. Amara is already planning where they'll graze.

entries.title: Victor Hale
entries.text: Victor Hale came in person. Good suit, good teeth, and an offer that sounded too good.

entries.title: Leopard country
entries.text: Tracks on the rocks and a kill up a fig tree. Tendai says there are two of them.

entries.title: Spotted
entries.text: We saw the leopard in daylight. Amara cried a little. So did I.

entries.title: Kito
entries.text: The rangers caught a boy carrying snares. He says a man in a truck pays him. A truck with no lights, on the east road.

entries.title: A footprint
entries.text: A rhino print by the north fence, wide as a plate. We have told no one.

entries.title: Something worth stealing
entries.text: Visitors, money, eight species and one rhino. For the first time, this place has something worth stealing.

entries.title: The outcrop
entries.text: The rocks in the north are ours again. The best view in the reserve, Tendai says.
